messages:
mark_acme: Hey team — after yesterday's model push our customer (Acme) is seeing large rank score changes on the rerank endpoint for the exact same payloads. They say previously doc A scored 0.82, now it's 0.56. Not a tiny float drift, this is breaking their sorting. Can someone look?

Aisha (CS): Ugh, thanks for flagging. Which model variant did we move them to? any canary? :eyes:

mark_acme: They were on `rerank-v2.1` and we rolled to `rerank-v2.2` as part of the push. No canary for their org — default rollout. I asked for full request & response, sent below (redacted ids):
```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "model": "rerank-v2.2",
  "queries": ["how to set up billing"],
  "candidates": ["docA","docB","docC"],
  "top_k": 5
}
```
Old scores (v2.1): `docA: 0.820`, `docB: 0.510`, `docC: 0.330`
New scores (v2.2): `docA: 0.562`, `docB: 0.588`, `docC: 0.345`

Aisha (CS): Thanks — that mismatch is big. Mateo, can you triage? Mark, can you confirm payload is identical bytes? any whitespace or encoding differences?

mark_acme: Confirmed identical JSON payload. I also attached a gzip of 100 sample requests that show similar score swings.

Mateo (ML Eng): I pulled one of the samples and re-ran locally against both model artifacts. Quick notes:
- With the v2.1 artifact I get `docA: 0.821`, same as reported.
- With v2.2 artifact I get `docA: 0.559`.
- The tokenization looks identical, same token ids.

Mateo (ML Eng): Two immediate hypotheses: quantization/kernel changes in v2.2 changed logits scaling, or we have nondeterministic behavior due to a different sampling/normalization op. Also need to check if we accidentally changed the score transform (logit->score mapping) in the serving layer.

Priya (SRE): Noted. I checked metrics around the deploy window: no infra failures but I do see a short burst of p50->p95 latency increase on rerank instances at 2026-03-12T21:04Z (deploy time). Could that have triggered fallback to a different runtime (xla vs cpu path) for some requests?

linkbot-deploy: Deploy event: service=rerank, image=rerank:2026-03-12-v2.2, rollout=100%, initiated by @deploy-ci, id=deploy-7890.

Mateo (ML Eng): Good catch Priya. If some pods are running an alternate runtime (e.g., quantized kernel vs fp16 path) you can get systematic score shifts. I'll dump model config and serving flags for the v2.2 pods.

Mateo (ML Eng): Quick dump from two pods:
```
pod-12: model_artifact=rerank-v2.2-quant, runtime_flags="use_fast_kernels=true, softmax_stable=true, score_scale=1.0"
pod-18: model_artifact=rerank-v2.2, runtime_flags="use_fast_kernels=false, softmax_stable=false, score_scale=0.68"
```
That mismatch is suspicious — pod-18 is applying a `score_scale` that would lower scores by ~0.68. Not sure why flags differ.

Priya (SRE): The autoscaler rolled up an extra pod during rollout and it appears the init container picked different runtime flags depending on available GPU arch. There's a bug in the rollout script where we don't pin the config to the model bundle. Oops. :grimacing:

Aisha (CS): So that explains the systematic drop for some requests. But why would docB go up relative to docA? Shouldn't scale affect all docs proportionally?

Mateo (ML Eng): True, a uniform multiplicative scale should preserve ordering. The per-doc non-uniform change suggests either 1) additional ops changed (e.g., improved normalization that penalizes longer docs differently), or 2) we have a softmax numeric stability difference that interacts with logits magnitudes. I'm running a per-layer compare for docA/docB to find the divergence.

Mark (Acme) (reply): Appreciate the quick look. They need a mitigation ASAP — current prod sorting is wrong for a subset of queries. Can we rollback them to v2.1?

Aisha (CS): Yes, we should offer rollback. Priya, can we pin Acme to v2.1 while we investigate?

Priya (SRE): I can create a per-org routing rule to pin `acme.com`->`rerank-v2.1` within 30 mins. Will also short-circuit the rollout script to avoid the config mismatch.

Mateo (ML Eng): Action plan I'm proposing:
1) Immediate: Priya pins Acme to v2.1 (safety rollback).
2) Short term: I will run head-to-head A/B on 10k queries to quantify distribution of score deltas (v2.1 vs v2.2).
3) Find root: compare serving flags, check model bundle metadata for `score_scale` and `norm_behavior` changes.
4) Fix: either unify serving flags or revert the change in v2.2 that altered normalization.
5) Long term: require canary and per-org pin in every rollout for first 24h.

Aisha (CS): Sounds good. Mark — I'll message the customer with the rollback and ETA. Will also ask for additional samples if they have them. :thumbsup:

Mateo (ML Eng): I ran the 10k test quick pass. Summary: 62% of queries show negligible delta (<0.01), 28% show moderate delta (0.01-0.1), 10% show large delta (>0.1). For the large-delta set, doc length and presence of special tokens correlate with drift.

Mateo (ML Eng): Raw snippet of the per-example logs (abbrev):
```
qhash: 0x1a3b, v2.1_scores: [0.82,0.51,0.33], v2.2_scores: [0.56,0.59,0.35], delta_top=-0.26, top_idx_v2.1=0, top_idx_v2.2=1
qhash: 0x2f0c, v2.1_scores: [0.72,0.70,0.69], v2.2_scores: [0.68,0.71,0.70], delta_top=-0.04, top_idx_v2.1=0, top_idx_v2.2=1
```

Priya (SRE): I pinned Acme to v2.1 routing and reverted the rollout config that caused mixed flags. Mark, you should see consistent results from your side in ~10 minutes.

mark_acme: Confirmed after 12 min — ordering looks back to normal on our samples. Thank you.

Aisha (CS): Great. Mateo, next steps for root cause? ETA?

Mateo (ML Eng): I'll finish the per-layer diffs and open a bug with priority P0 if we find serving flag drift. Early hypothesis: model bundle metadata omitted the `norm_behavior` field, causing older default to be used on some pods. If that's true, fix is to update bundle + force-config. ETA for initial RCA: 24h.

Aisha (CS): Please add remediation doc and a postmortem once resolved. We'll author a short customer-facing note explaining what happened and the rollback.

Mateo (ML Eng): Will do. I've created ticket INF-1427 and assigned to myself and Priya. Attachments: diff patch, sample logs, 10k-stats csv.

Priya (SRE): I'll follow up to add canary gating to deployment playbook and make the per-org pinning a runbook step.

mark_acme: Thanks everyone. For transparency could you include the raw diff and the list of sample qhashes we used? We'll share internally with product team.

Aisha (CS): Yep — I'll attach the sanitized artifacts to the support ticket and share timeline. Closing here once we have RCA + postmortem. :white_check_mark:

linkbot-deploy: Rollback event: service=rerank, target=rerank-v2.1 for org=acme.com, initiated by @Priya.

Mateo (ML Eng): Quick note for the follow-up: check numeric casts in the scoring layer (float32->float16) and the softmax implementation across kernels. Those are frequent sources of non-uniform deltas.

Priya (SRE): Noted. I'll also add an alert rule for score-distribution shifts > 0.08 at critical orgs.

Aisha (CS): Thanks team, keeping this thread for the chronology.
